gap_description: What it does: Controlled Docker actions list containers, restart, pull, tail logs, inspect health, manage compose stacks. Why You currently have query_service_logs and bash execution, but a structured docker tool is safer and easier to reason about than raw shell.
purpose: Provides structured Docker management without raw shell access. Safer and easier to reason about than execute_bash for Docker operations.
capabilities: List all containers with status and health
Tail container logs with line limits
Manage Docker Compose stacks (up, down, restart, pull)

parameters.action: Action to perform: 'list' (show containers), 'restart' (restart container), 'pull' (pull image), 'logs' (view logs), 'inspect' (health check), 'stats' (resource usage), 'compose' (manage compose stacks)
parameters.container: Container name or ID (required for restart, logs, inspect, stats actions)
parameters.image: Docker image name with optional tag (required for pull action, e.g., 'nginx:latest')
parameters.lines: Number of log lines to retrieve (default: 50, used with logs action)
parameters.all: Show all containers including stopped ones (default: false, used with list action)
parameters.compose_action: Docker Compose action (required for compose action): 'up' (start), 'down' (stop), 'restart', 'pull' (update images), 'ps' (list), 'logs'
parameters.compose_file: Path to docker-compose.yml file (optional, defaults to ./docker-compose.yml)
